The '''2024 Toronto Argonauts season''' was the 66th season for the team in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and their 151st year of existence. The [[Toronto Argonauts|Argonauts]] qualified for the playoffs for the fourth consecutive year with a win on October 11 over the [[2024 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|Winnipeg Blue Bombers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2024/10/11/argonauts-beat-bombers-to-punch-playoff-ticket/ |title=Argonauts beat Bombers to punch playoff ticket |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=October 11, 2024}}</ref> The team won their 19th [[Grey Cup]] championship after defeating the Blue Bombers in the [[111th Grey Cup]] game.

The [[2024 CFL season]] was the fourth season for [[head coach]] [[Ryan Dinwiddie]] and the fifth season for [[Michael Clemons]] as [[general manager]].<ref name="Argos HC">{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2019/12/12/ryan-dinwiddie-named-45th-head-coach-argos-history/|title=Ryan Dinwiddie named 45th head coach in Argos history|work=[[Toronto Argonauts]]|date=December 12, 2019|access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=CFL.ca Staff |title=Argos relieve GM Jim Popp of duties |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/10/08/report-argos-relieve-gm-jim-popp-duties/ |publisher=CFL.ca |date=October 8, 2019 |access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref>

On July 11, 2024, team owners, [[Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment]] (MLSE), parted ways with team president, [[Bill Manning]], and stated that Clemons would report directly to MLSE President, [[Keith Pelley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2024/07/11/mlse-and-bill-manning-president-of-tfc-and-argonauts-mutually-agree-to-part-ways/ |title=MLSE and Bill Manning, President of TFC and Argonauts, mutually agree to part ways |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=July 11, 2024}}</ref>

The Toronto Argonauts drew an average home attendance of 15,129 in 2024.

==Offseason==
===CFL global draft===
The [[2024 CFL global draft]] took place on April 30, 2024.<ref name=highlight>{{cite web|url=https://press.cfl.ca/cfl-combine-in-winnipeg-and-april-30-drafts-highlight-2024-offseason |title=CFL Combine in Winnipeg and April 30 drafts highlight 2024 offseason |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=January 31, 2024}}</ref> The Argonauts had two picks in the draft, selecting seventh in each round.<ref name=2024Global>{{cite news|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2024-global-draft-tracker/ |title=2024 Global draft tracker |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 5, 2024}}</ref>

==CFL national draft==
The [[2024 CFL draft]] took place on April 30, 2024.<ref name=highlight/> The Argonauts had nine selections in the eight-round draft.<ref name=2024National>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/draft-tracker/2024/ |title=Draft tracker |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 5, 2024}}</ref> Through a series of trades with [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats|Hamilton]] and [[Edmonton Elks|Edmonton]], the Argonauts improved their first-round pick by two spots, and had three selections in the third round and two each in the fifth and sixth rounds.<ref name=2024National/>

==Preseason==
The Argonauts' home preseason game was played at [[Alumni Stadium (Guelph)|Alumni Stadium]] in [[Guelph]], [[Ontario]].<ref name=Argoschedule>{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2023/12/14/argos-announce-2024-schedule/ |title=Argos announce 2024 schedule |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=December 14, 2023}}</ref>

==Regular season==
===Standings===
{{2024 CFL East Division standings}}

===Schedule===
The Argonauts are scheduled to play nine regular season home games in Toronto for the first time since [[2018 Toronto Argonauts season|2018]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://members.argonauts.ca/ |title=Argos membership central |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref> The team was the designated host for [[Touchdown Atlantic]] games in [[2019 Toronto Argonauts season|2019]], [[2022 Toronto Argonauts season|2022]], and [[2023 Toronto Argonauts season|2023]], while the [[2020 CFL season]] was cancelled and the [[2021 CFL season]] had every team hosting seven home games.
